Medical Service Company (MSC) isn't just another healthcare operator. It's a third-generation, family-owned durable medical equipment provider with 78 years of earned trust and a presence across seven states. MSC has built its reputation specializing in sleep and respiratory disease management, partnering with health systems to streamline discharge and outpatient needs.

MSC's intake process was overloaded with manual work. Every order required one staff member to wrestle the entire workflow from end-to-end: fax retrieval, phone follow-ups with referral sources, EHR navigation, insurance determinations, benefits management, and sales order creation. All for a single patient. The resulting process was slow and created scaling problems.
The math on growth was clear: the only way to handle more volume was to hire more people.
Seth said. The platform's growth velocity and the team's responsiveness were the signals that Seth saw as proof that Tennr was a partner worth building with.
Life with Tennr: Assembly line process put on Autopilot

The transformation didn't happen by bolting “AI” onto the existing process. Together with Tennr's change management team, MSC designed its intake workflows as a modular assembly line—breaking the monolithic "one person does everything" model into specialized, automatable stages. And with Tennr’s Autopilot, entire steps in that workflow now complete without a human ever touching them.

The rote, manual tasks that ate up hours every day—splitting faxed documents into prescriptions, progress notes, and sleep studies; classifying thousands of pages; routing work to the right team members—began happening automatically.
MSC now processes all of their orders, 2.4 million pages annually, through Tennr
The 20-minute order creation slog? Down to approximately 2 minutes of active work time with no drop in accuracy.

Infusion providers sit at the end of a long chain in the healthcare system, inheriting everything that went wrong upstream. Incomplete referrals arriving by fax, unclear payer policy, new-to-market drugs without coverage guidelines, and contracting that dictates how a drug must be billed and authorized land on the intake team.

On top of that, infusion admin teams carry the responsibility of communicating and coordinating with patients and their prescribers. As Michelle Butler, Project Manager at TwelveStone put it, that results in her team playing the roles of social worker, translator, and caregiver on the way to getting a patient on therapy in a timely manner.
"It feels like we've been working with you guys forever," Michelle said. "It's a good marriage."

"Because [medical policy review] is part of the flow and Tennr already does the validation with the Qualification Review Engine, it really does give you a cleaner authorization submission. When it was a person doing it, if they missed something, it could result in a denial.” — Michelle

TwelveStone expects to reach 40 infusion centers by the end of the year, with 20 more clinics planned for the year after. The referrals will still arrive by fax, still incomplete. The patients will still be sick, frightened, and unsure who is calling them. None of that is TwelveStone's to fix.

. Tennr’s sales cycle began to accelerate when they were able to lead with examples of ROI and case studies in the pitch to close customers. Perhaps controversially, Tennr has actually stripped AI from their homepage and focused on what matters: fewer denials, more patient conversions, and real revenue impact.

Shortly after hitting $1M in ARR, Trey made a hard call: fire 60% of Tennr’s customers, because they just weren’t aligned with Tennr’s core value prop. Serving the wrong ICP drains time, slows roadmap velocity, and muddles the story.

As a founder, there is a balance between focus and staying informed on the market — Trey continues to talk to non-ICP potential customers to explore future revenue streams. But this is specific to founders — Trey operates his team against the focused KPIs and milestones for the near-term.
Don’t be afraid to hone in — a short-term dip in revenue is well worthwhile for long-term growth.
